extracted.intended_audience: writers, screenwriters, storytelling students, and researchers interested in Robert McKee and his teaching
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Robert McKee's teaching criteria and guidance about storytelling, screenwriting structure, style, genre conventions, and seminar formats as described on his Wikipedia page. Useful for writers learning McKee's approach or researchers cataloging storycraft standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee's three-day Story Seminar teaches writers McKee's principles of storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Story Seminar is a three-day, 30-hour intensive class (originally a USC course opened to the public) that presents McKee's overarching principles; many of these are collected in his book Story. Seminars have been held worldwide and form the core delivery of his teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance (as a screenwriting criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the core headings of McKee's book: 'Story: Substance, Structure, Style and the Principles of Screenwriting' — substance as a primary component of good storycraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the material — what the story is about, its thematic weight and the seriousness of its dramatic premises — as a distinct evaluative dimension (paired with structure and style in McKee's framework). The book is used as required reading in many film/cinema programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure (as a screenwriting criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure is a named, central element of McKee's framework ('Story: Substance, Structure, Style and the Principles of Screenwriting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes classical/architectural organization of story (plot progression, beats, turning points) grounded in sources such as Aristotle and Kenneth Thorpe Rowe; structure is presented as a discipline writers must master rather than ignore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style (as a screenwriting criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Style is explicitly listed alongside substance and structure in McKee's principal framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns choices of language, tone, and the craft of verbal/action expression on stage, page, and screen (see McKee's other books such as Dialogue and Character for extended guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee's one-day Genre Seminars 'teach writers McKee's take on the conventions of different styles of storytelling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genres explicitly cited include love story, thriller, comedy, horror, action, and writing for television. The metric is how well a piece uses or understands the established conventions of its declared genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voice-over (anti-pattern and allowed pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee teaches that 'using voice-over to substitute for telling the story via action and dialogue is weak' while 'voice-over used to counterpoint and enrich the story can be wonderful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate voice-over by whether it substitutes for dramatic action (bad) or provides counterpoint/enrichment (good). This is an explicit practical rule McKee emphasizes in seminars and Q&A commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict and drama / fundamentals
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee emphasizes fundamentals of storytelling such as conflict and drama, tracing many ideas to Aristotle and earlier dramatists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence, escalation, and resolution of conflict and the deliberate shaping of dramatic action are core evaluative criteria in McKee's teaching; he frames these as long-standing fundamentals writers have lost touch with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of storytelling to business (Storynomics)
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee's Storynomics Seminar teaches 'the application of storytelling principles in the business and marketing world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating story-driven marketing or corporate narratives, measure how storytelling principles are applied to business goals (engagement, persuasion) rather than strictly artistic aims. This seminar is co-lectured with Tom Gerace and targets business/marketing audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to established storytelling structures (skepticism of breaking conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee's approach has been characterized as showing 'hostility' toward screenwriting practices that challenge or break conventions; he favors established structural norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under McKee's framework, deviation from conventional structure is treated skeptically; evaluate innovations against whether they undermine dramatic fundamentals rather than as intrinsically positive. Critics describe this as a conservative stance toward narrative experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar intensity and teaching format as quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: McKee's Story Seminar is delivered as a three-day, 30-hour intensive; his Genre and Storynomics offerings are one-day seminars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The format (intensive multi-day vs single-day) implies depth and scope of coverage: the three-day seminar covers core storytelling principles in depth, while one-day seminars focus on genre conventions or applications. For producers of teaching materials, match depth to format expectations.
